public.title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
public.description: Convert a strictly increasing array of 0 to 200 integers between -10000 and 10000 into a height-balanced binary search tree. To make the result unique, choose the lower middle index of every inclusive subarray as its root, then recurse on both sides. Return compact breadth-first serialization, retaining interior nulls and removing all trailing nulls. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: read the root, then left and right child slots for each non-null node in queue order. null marks a missing child; absent trailing slots are null. [] is empty. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000 and there are at most 200 nodes.
hints: Splitting at the lower middle fixes an otherwise ambiguous output.
Queue nodes including null slots when serializing.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026, for a standard algorithmic problem. No third-party exercise text or solution code used.

explanation: A midpoint split keeps subtree heights within one. Recursively build the tree and serialize with BFS. O(n) time and O(n) space.
